Subject: Severe latency spike this morning impacting production

Hi Mina,

We started seeing a large number of timeouts and very high p95/p99 latencies against the hosted-api around 08:45 PDT. Our telemetry shows request latencies for embeddings and chat endpoints jumping from ~120ms p95 to >1.2s p95 and p99 approaching 4s for several minutes. This caused retries and a visible slowdown in our search UI.

We rely on your hosted endpoints for real-time features — this is customer-impacting. Can you confirm if this is an isolated client-side issue or a platform regression? We need a post-incident note and ETA for mitigation.

Attaching our sample traces and query IDs for the window: query-samples-20270520.json

—Jenny

Subject: Re: Severe latency spike this morning impacting production

TL;DR: We saw a brief surge in tail latency tied to a bad kernel scheduling decision on a small subset of serving hosts while a high-variance traffic pattern hit the large-sequence generation path. Steps taken: removed affected hosts from rotation, forced cache warm on remaining nodes, and tightened batching window until a fix lands.

Details:
- 08:43–08:52 PDT: p95 increased from ~0.12s to ~1.2s; p99 peaked ~3.9s for ~6 minutes.
- Affected pool: hosted-eu-west-2a-optimized (note: customer routed to nearest region via geo-fallback) — a minority of requests were routed there due to a transient routing imbalance.
- Root cause (prelim): kernel thread scheduling + quantization codepath interaction causing longer-than-expected kernel queues under a short, very spiky workload.

Mitigation performed (09:05):
- Removed 6 hosts, rebalanced traffic.
- Applied emergency process-level backpressure and narrowed batching window; this restored p95 to baseline by 09:12.

Next steps: we’re preparing a code patch and will coordinate with CloudCo (kernel vendor) if required. I’ll paste logs and a short timeline to the incident doc.

Marcus
Marcus Lin

Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 16:12:05 -07:00
Subject: Postmortem: p95/p99 regression on hosted-api (INC-20270520-1)

Hi Jenny — attaching the postmortem draft (postmortem-hostedapi-p95-regression-draft.pdf) and a short executive summary below. Thanks again for your patience.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2027-05-20 08:43–08:52 PDT.
- Impact: brief but high tail latencies (p95 up ~1.1s; p99 up ~3.9s) affecting ~4% of requests across multi-tenant hosted pools. Several customers (including Acme) experienced retries and client-visible slowdowns.
- Root cause: interaction between a kernel-level scheduling regression on a small subset of serving hosts and our large-sequence generation quantized codepath under spiky traffic.
- Immediate remediation: affected hosts removed, batching window tightened, cache warm forced.
- Long-term fixes: kernel vendor engagement; patch to scheduling heuristics; improved health-checking and automated host quarantine thresholds; expanded tail-latency canaries in canary suite.

Planned follow-ups (owners + ETA):
- Code patch and staged rollout: Marcus/Connor — 5 business days.
- Vendor coordination and kernel patch (if required): Ops — 10 business days.
- Billing credit proposal: Laura/Billing — 3 business days.
- Customer debrief (technical): 30–45 minute session; available Tue/Wed next week.

If this looks good I’ll finalize and publish the customer-facing postmortem and update the status timeline.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
